text: Jean-Marie Hullot (February 16, 1954 – June 17, 2019) was a French computer scientist and programmer known for creating significant software for the original Macintosh, NeXTSTEP, and Mac OS X platforms. He developed the SOS Interface for the Mac, which later became Interface Builder for NeXTSTEP in 1985 and eventually became a key component of Mac OS X. He also contributed to the conception of the iPhone, though did not play a major role in its development, and led the iCal and iSync development teams for Mac OS X starting in 2002. In 1981, Hullot earned a Ph.D. in computer science from the University of Paris at Orsay, with Gérard Huet as his adviser. He worked as a researcher at INRIA from 1979 to 1985 before joining NeXT. In 1996, he co-founded RealNames, a URL translation service that ceased operations in 2002. From 2001 to 2005, he served as CTO of the application division at Apple Inc. He was also the president and CEO of Fotopedia, a collaborative photo encyclopedia, and co-founded The Iris Foundation, a nature conservancy organization. He passed away on June 19, 2019.
